newsitem.title: USA: Nine-airline pact would pose little threat.
newsitem.headline: Nine-airline pact would pose little threat.

text.p: A sweeping network being formed by nine airlines will pose little threat to rival carriers since it merely adds to an already powerful alliance, analysts said.
An Air Canada official told Reuters in London that nine airlines are forming an alliance to counter the threat posed by the proposed link between British Airways Plc and AMR Corp's American Airlines.
The grouping would build upon the broad alliance between UAL Corp, Deutsche Lufthansa AG and Scandinavian Airlines System.
"The core alliance already exists. It makes sense that they would add to that alliance to increase the cities they can serve," said Jeffrey Long, an analyst with J.P. Morgan Securities.
United also has relationships with Air Canada, Airlines of Britain Holdings Plc and Thai International.
Other airlines, such as Brazil's Varig, All Nippon Airways Co Ltd and South African Airways, would likely join the alliance, sources told Reuters.
"This is nothing new. It's more of the same. Basically, what they're saying is that they'll offer a seamless travel experience," said Julius Maldutis, an analyst with Salomon Brothers.
A United Airlines spokesman in the U.S. said the company has explored options with various airlines, but it had no announcement about expanding its existing family of carriers.

Rival U.S. airlines declined to comment until a formal announcement has been made. British Airways said the report of the of nine-carrier alliance only strengthened the case for its proposed deal with American.
